message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **federal public holidays** in Canada for 2023 that create *long weekends* (i.e., the holiday falls on a Monday–Thursday, so you can take the adjacent weekend days off).  
(Provincial/territorial holidays that fall on a weekday also create long weekends, but they vary by region – see the “Regional notes” section.)

| Date | Holiday | Day of Week | Long Weekend? | Notes |
|------|---------|-------------|---------------|-------|
| Jan 1 2023 | New Year’s Day | Sun | **Yes** (Saturday Dec 31 & Sunday Jan 1) | Federal holiday; automatically a long weekend. |
| Feb 20 2023 | Family Day (Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | Mon | **Yes** | Only in those provinces/territories. |
| Mar 17 2023 | Good Friday | Fri | **Yes** (Fri Mar 17 + Sat Mar 18 + Sun Mar 19) | Federal holiday; always a long weekend. |
| Apr 7 2023 | Easter Monday (Federal employees only) | Mon | **Yes** (Mon Apr 7 + Sat Apr 8 + Sun Apr 9) | Not a public holiday for most Canadians, but a long weekend for federal workers. |
| May 22 2023 | Victoria Day | Mon | **Yes** (Mon May 22 + Sat May 20 + Sun May 21) | Federal holiday; long weekend. |
| Jul 1 2023 | Canada Day | Tue | **Yes** (Sat Jun 30 + Sun Jul 1 + Mon Jul 2) | Federal holiday; long weekend. |
| Sep 4 2023 | Labour Day | Mon | **Yes** (Mon Sep 4 + Sat Sep 2 + Sun Sep 3) | Federal holiday; long weekend. |
| Oct 9 2023 | Thanksgiving | Mon | **Yes** (Mon Oct 9 + Sat Oct 7 + Sun Oct 8) | Federal holiday; long weekend. |
| Nov 11 2023 | Remembrance Day | Wed | **Yes** (Wed Nov 11 + Sat Nov 10 + Sun Nov 11) | Federal holiday; long weekend. |
| Dec 25 2023 | Christmas Day | Mon | **Yes** (Mon Dec 25 + Sat Dec 23 + Sun Dec 24) | Federal holiday; long weekend. |
| Dec 26 2023 | Boxing Day | Tue | **Yes** (Tue Dec 26 + Sat Dec 23 + Sun Dec 24) | Federal holiday; long weekend. |

### How to use this in your app
1. **Create a calendar view** that highlights the above dates.  
2. **Add a filter** for “Long Weekend” so users can quickly see which holidays give them extra days off.  
3. **Include a tooltip** or modal that explains the rule: “If the holiday falls on a Monday–Thursday, you can take the adjacent weekend days off.”  
4. **Provide a link** to the official Government of Canada page for holiday rules: https://www.canada.ca/en/services/finance/public-holidays.html

### Regional notes
- **Family Day** is observed in Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, and Ontario.  
- **St. Patrick’s Day** (Mar 17) is a statutory holiday in Newfoundland and Labrador.  
- **St. George’s Day** (Jun 23) is a statutory holiday in Prince Edward Island.  
- **Civic Holiday** (first Monday in August) is observed in most provinces except Quebec.  
- **Natal Day** (first Monday in August) is observed in Nova Scotia.  
- **National Indigenous Peoples Day** (June 21) is a statutory holiday in Yukon.  

These regional holidays also create long weekends when they fall on a Monday–Thursday. If you want to support all provinces/territories, you’ll need to maintain a separate list per region.

---

**Quick tip:** If you’re building a holiday‑planning feature, consider using an API such as the *Calendarific* or *Date.nager* services, which return holiday data in JSON format and let you filter by country, year, and type (public, bank, etc.). This will keep your data up‑to‑date without manual maintenance.
